properties.name: MEASURED: capture is blind to families two ways — three node types no skill can reach at all, and two more (Constraint, Flow) the routing table names and the design still routes into prose
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-14 on reflow2's own committed export (4,477 nodes, 26,622 edges) and the 27 served skills, at Anthony's direction, as option (b) of the decision this hangs on. The storyflow question — "is a monolithic capture blind to whole families?" — answered on this design, without an LLM in the loop: three deterministic cuts and one calibrated proxy.

═══ CUT 1 — STRUCTURAL REACH: which node types can ANY skill route to? ═══
For every node type with a typed constructor, which SKILL.md names that tool:
  · Actor (add_actor) — NO skill. None of 27. 3 Actors in the design.
  · EnvironmentRule (add_environment_rule) — NO skill. 0 nodes.
  · ReadinessAssessment (add_readiness) — NO skill. 0 nodes.
  · Flow (add_flow) — capture-intent ONLY. 1 Flow in 4,477 nodes.
  · Component (add_component) — capture-intent ONLY. 108.
  · Constraint — capture-intent, kpp-proposal, optimize. 8.
  · Interface — four skills. 22.
  · Requirement / Capability / Decision — four to five skills each. 226 / 254 / 709.
This is the direct analogue of storyflow's "the monolith fired zero hierarchy edges": a type no instruction points at is created only by accident. ACTOR IS THE STARK ONE — the vocabulary has a type for who the system serves, and no served skill ever says to use it.

═══ CUT 2 — YIELD: what the design actually holds ═══
Flow 1 (0.02%), PART_OF_FLOW 8 edges. Constraint 8. Actor 3. Environment 3. Resource 1. DECOMPOSES 0 edges — the decomposition_coverage detector has never had anything to run on. Interface 22, and the skill's "record BOTH sides of every contract" yielded PROVIDES 18 against CONSUMES 56 — three to one, the rule followed on one side.
Documents captured FROM (36 artifacts with DOCUMENTS edges, 54 nodes yielded): Decision 18, Project 9, TemporalFact 8, Release 8, Capability 5, Component 3, Requirement 2, Interface 1, and Flow / Constraint / Actor ZERO. Every document reading produced records and rulings; none produced a process, a prohibition, or a served party.

═══ CUT 3 — GROUND TRUTH BY THE TABLE'S OWN TRIGGERS, with measured precision ═══
The routing table in capture-intent names the phrasing that routes to each type. Regex for that phrasing over every node's prose, then a random sample of 10 matches read by hand to calibrate:
  · CONSTRAINT row ("we must never…", "it is not allowed to…" → Constraint, NOT a Requirement): 68 nodes match. Sample precision 9/10 — genuine design prohibitions ("a non-tty must never hang", "the report must never become telemetry", "the edge must never become RESOLVES", "an absolute path must never enter a global config"). ≈61 prohibitions living in the prose of Decisions (22), Requirements (14), Capabilities (10) and change records — against 8 Constraint nodes. ⭐ AND THIS IS THE ROW THE TABLE ADDED PRECISELY BECAUSE "eleven constitutional prohibitions [were] left as Requirements" — the row exists, and the design went on routing prohibitions into prose anyway.
  · FLOW row ("first this, then that" → Flow): 166 match. Sample precision ~2–3/10 — most hits are "step 5 of the skill" references or history narrated as "first… then". The genuine ones are the coherence loop's own ordered sequence ("change event first, then the durable intent"), the release cut, the detect→ask handshake. Even at 10% precision that is ≈16 ordered processes against 1 Flow node; at the sampled rate, ≈40.
  · ACTOR ("the user", "an operator who…", a served party): 389 match — the proxy is too loose to count on (this design talks about "the user" constantly), so no ratio is claimed; the structural cut already settles Actor.
  · INTERFACE ("where X meets Y", "the contract between", "handoff"): 44 match vs 22 nodes — not a blind family; the one-sided PROVIDES/CONSUMES is the defect there.

═══ ⭐ THE FINDING, IN ONE SENTENCE ═══
Capture is blind two different ways, and only one of them is a missing instruction: ACTOR, EnvironmentRule and ReadinessAssessment are unreachable because nothing points at them; CONSTRAINT and FLOW are unreached although capture-intent's table has a row for each — instruction present, yield ≈ zero, nothing noticing. That second shape is the three-leg rule again (tool ✓, instruction ✓, detector ✗), and it is the same shape the promotion edge had this morning.

═══ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══
Per-type RECALL of an agent running the skill on a brief with known answers — the storyflow number. This design is a self-host (ChangeEvent, Decision and TemporalFact are 49% of nodes), so its prose is dominated by records of building, and a product design might route differently. The Flow proxy is weak and is reported with its precision rather than as a count. The usage ledger on this box spans two days and 623 calls (add_flow 0, add_interface 0, add_component 0, add_actor 0) — consistent, but a window of the author's own sessions, so supporting only. Establishing recall needs a corpus with known answers, and Alex's pseudo-project is still the candidate.
